faq.q: Does the body replace itself every seven years?
faq.a: No, that is a myth. Different cells are replaced at different speeds: some in days, some over years, and some, like most brain nerve cells and the eye lens, last a lifetime.
asks: Are we new people every seven years?

faq.q: How often is the gut lining replaced?
faq.a: The cells lining the inside of the small intestine are replaced about every three to five days, made by stem cells deep in tiny pits in the gut wall.
asks: Why are gut cells replaced so fast?
How long do gut cells live?

faq.q: How long does it take to renew the skeleton?
faq.a: Bone is constantly broken down and rebuilt by bone cells. In adults this remodelling replaces roughly the whole skeleton over about ten years.
Most nerve cells in the brain, the cells in the centre of the eye's lens and the egg cells in the ovaries are with a person for life. Heart muscle cells are replaced only very slowly.

faq.q: Why are some cells replaced faster than others?
faq.a: Cells that face wear and tear, like gut lining and skin, are replaced quickly. Cells that store a lifetime of connections, like brain nerve cells, last much longer.
asks: Why do gut cells die quickly?
What decides how long a cell lives?

facts: Cells lining the small intestine are replaced roughly every three to five days.
The adult skeleton is replaced through remodelling about every ten years.
Carbon dating of DNA has shown that most nerve cells in the human cerebral cortex are as old as the person.

quiz.say: Which of these is replaced the fastest?
quiz.why: Gut lining cells face constant wear from food and digestive juices and are replaced every few days.

wrong.1: The skeleton takes about ten years to renew.
wrong.2: Lens cells in the centre of the eye last a lifetime.
